footnote: Sources: Guancha, China Music Business News, Jiemian, CCTV News, Legal Daily (citing the China Consumers' Association), Beijing police
notes: Risks and Plan B. All six risks have happened in the past two years. Weather: in July 2026 Typhoon Bavi cancelled three G.E.M. shows in Hangzhou, and the promoter refunded tickets and covered travel and hotels. In May a gale damaged the stage at the Bubble Island festival in Tianjin. Our station kit can move to another city, and vouchers follow the new date. Execution: at Genki Forest's own Beijing festival on 1 May 2025 a band arrived late, the headline set shrank from the advertised 30 minutes to about seven, the crowd chanted for refunds and the brand's social account was swamped. When a brand runs the festival, the brand takes the blame, so we will not run one. Promoters run the stage and we run the stations outside. Artists: after the Zhang Zhehan affair in August 2021, Wahaha cut ties first and 26 brands followed within 4 hours 21 minutes. We sign show-level deals only, no endorsements, with a morals clause, and take every asset down within four hours if needed. Scalpers: a ring in Zhenjiang grabbed more than 60,000 tickets in two years and made over RMB 16 million. Prize tickets are real-name, so the winner is the person who attends. Refunds: the China Consumers' Association says concert complaints doubled in the first half of 2025 and more than 90% concerned refunds, so prize-ticket refund rules are set out in advance. The last one is ours alone: Beijing police listed bottled drinks as banned at large events over the 2026 Dragon Boat holiday. That is a Beijing notice, not a national rule, but our default is freshly made cups finished on the spot.
